transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-31 16:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Sharma (Redwood) - Mark Thompson, Lina Rodriguez, Samir Khan, Olivia Park (Evergreen HR)

Summary: quick run through of SSO SAML setup options, SCIM provisioning and RBAC roles; discussion about audit logs, retention, KMS, data residency and SOC 2 evidence.

00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a friday, appreciate it, um we'll run through the SSO and scim flow and then the role-based access model suggestions we've seen work well for HR platforms.
00:18 Mark Thompson: thanks jordan, quick background, we're migrating a bunch of HR tooling into a central platform and want to lock down access. we already use okta and azure ad depending on team. major ask: least privilege, separation for admins, and full audit trails for compliance auditors.
00:36 Priya Sharma: great, okta / azure ad are both supported; high level we do two integration patterns: SAML/IDP for login + SCIM for user and group provisioning, or OIDC + SCIM if you prefer. SAML is most common for SSO in enterprise.
00:52 Lina Rodriguez: we leaned on saml for other vendors, scim sometimes flaky. how do you handle group sync conflicts and deprovisioning?
01:12 Priya Sharma: good question. SCIM provisioning is idempotent: we map external groups to Redwood groups, we surface conflict logs in the console and via audit logs. for deprovisioning we support immediate disable and optional hard delete after retention window; typically customers choose disable + 30 day purge. there can be race conditions if multiple sources write, we advise single source of truth.
01:37 Samir Khan: what about service accounts, automation, and least privilege? we want separate admin accounts for platform operators vs devs.
01:52 Jordan Lee: yes we recommend role tiers: super-admin (very limited), security-admin (can view audit & logs), ops-admin (deploy/rollout controls), developer (model and route configs), viewer. super-admin is normally a small SSO-managed group with MFA enforced.
02:12 Olivia Park: and for HR ops folks we only want access to user management for the HR app, not model configs.
02:21 Priya Sharma: that's achievable via RBAC mapping: map HR groups to 'user-manager' role with only SCIM / user endpoints access, no deploy. you can also restrict token scopes and issue scoped API keys.
02:38 Mark Thompson: audit logs are critical. retention and tamper-evidence? our auditors ask for 1 year of immutable logs. do you support that?
02:52 Priya Sharma: Redwood stores audit trails for admin actions and API calls. by default retention is 90 days for hosted customers; for enterprise we offer configurable retention (365 days or more) and can ship logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export. immutability is by using WORM S3 buckets or sending to your log archival. we also support signed audit entries for additional verification.
03:20 Samir Khan: encryption and KMS — do you provide customer-managed keys for encryption at rest? we need to ensure keys are rotated and we have A/V for key access.
03:33 Jordan Lee: yes, enterprise private deployments and some dedicated customers can use customer-managed KMS (cloud KMS or HSM). keys encrypt model artifacts, token caches, and stored prompts. Key rotation supported; we log key usage in audit logs.
03:50 Lina Rodriguez: data residency — some employees' PII must stay in eu-region, is regional deployment an option?
04:03 Priya Sharma: we support region pinning for hosted; also private deployments in VPC with data residency guarantees. For hosted, you can choose EU region and we will route and store data there. note: some backups may be cross-region unless you pick a private deployment package.
04:26 Mark Thompson: SOC 2 and ISO evidence: how do you provide artifacts for auditors?
04:35 Priya Sharma: we provide SOC 2 reports under NDA; our control mappings and audit artifacts can be exported. for ISO, we share relevant policies. we also provide per-tenant logs and change history as part of the enterprise package.
04:52 Samir Khan: SCIM provisioning: what attributes do you map? we want user.title, department, manager, employeeId, and groups for access control.
05:05 Priya Sharma: standard SCIM attributes are supported; custom attribute mapping is available for enterprise. groups map to roles; we can do attribute-based access where manager field can map to approval flows.
05:22 Olivia Park: how quickly does deprovisioning reflect? if someone leaves, we need immediate revoke of access to the HR app.
:05:33 Jordan Lee: if you push deprovision via SCIM immediate disable happens in under a minute typically; long-lived tokens are revoked on next check or can be forcibly expired via admin revoke.
05:45 Mark Thompson: okay what about test plan — we want a full integration test: SAML login, SCIM group create, user create, deprovision, and audit log verification.
06:02 Priya Sharma: we can provide a demo tenant and a test harness. priya: (slight audio glitch) i'll set up scim demo and provide creds.
06:15 Samir Khan: any gotchas with SAML metadata? our idp requires signed responses and audience restrictions.
06:28 Jordan Lee: supported — we accept signed assertions, encrypted assertions optional; audience and recipient checks are enforced. we also have logs for assertion failures to help debug.
06:45 Lina Rodriguez: are there role-based constraints on API keys? can we create scoped API keys per team?
06:55 Priya Sharma: yes, scoped keys per route and model. plus token TTLs and revoke. recommended to use short TTLs for high-privilege keys.
07:10 Mark Thompson: competitor question: some vendors only offer SCIM in their premium tier — what's your stance?
07:20 Jordan Lee: SCIM and enterprise RBAC are part of our enterprise plan; we also do custom SLAs for dedicated/private deployments.
07:30 Olivia Park: regarding least-privilege, can we get a sample role mapping template?
07:36 Priya Sharma: yes we'll share a role mapping template (csv) that maps idp groups to Redwood roles and suggested permissions.
07:48 Samir Khan: logging — are sensitive fields redacted in logs? we cannot have full PII in plaintext logs.
07:58 Priya Sharma: good point. we redact PII in application logs and provide redaction config. audit logs include action metadata but not raw PII; where necessary we can provide hashed identifiers.
08:15 Mark Thompson: what about compliance for third-party subprocessors? we need a list for our vendor risk team.
08:24 Jordan Lee: we have a subprocessors list and DPA; will include that in the security package.
08:32 Olivia Park: SCIM groups mapping — can we auto-provision groups based on AD group names?
08:40 Priya Sharma: yes, exact match or regex mapping is supported. you can also map multiple AD groups to a single Redwood role.
08:50 Samir Khan: any rate limits on SCIM? our HR sync can do bulk changes during offboarding windows.
08:58 Priya Sharma: there are rate limits to protect the platform; for enterprise we can raise them or provide a bulk import endpoint for one-time large syncs.
09:12 Mark Thompson: for the audit trail export, can we get a streaming option or do you do periodic exports?
09:20 Priya Sharma: both — streaming to SIEM (syslog/cef) or periodic S3 exports. streaming gives near real-time.
09:30 Samir Khan: do you support SCIM does delta syncs?
09:34 Priya Sharma: yes, incremental deltas are supported, full syncs too.
09:40 Mark Thompson: ok final - what are the immediate next steps?
09:44 Jordan Lee: action items: share docs, set up demo tenant, customer to send role matrix. schedule follow up in 2 weeks for integration test.
09:54 Priya Sharma: i'll create the scim demo and send creds, i'll also attach sample role mapping csv and retention options.
10:05 Mark Thompson: thanks all, appreciate the recap. we'll review internally and Samir will coordinate with auditors on retention specifics.
10:12 Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, happy new year early, we'll follow up on the action items.

Notes / artifacts referenced: https://redwood.example.com/docs/sso-integration (SSO guide), https://redwood.example.com/docs/scim-provisioning (SCIM guide), shared role-mapping-template.csv (to be attached).

End of transcript.
